html:
Theory earns the questions; practice passes the exam. This phase collects the full-lab practical battery: timed Apex exercises mirroring the certification scenario style, and three mini projects that assemble Phases 1–14 around real Salesforce automation. Run them in the scratch org this repo deploys, then grade yourself against the answer key.

Learning Objectives

By the end of this phase, you will be able to:

  • Execute the six signature labs end-to-end against the deployed scratch org.
  • Build the three mini projects (consent-aware activation, real-time churn handler, Agentforce grounding context) using this repo's services as skeletons.
  • Prove 75%+ coverage on the lab's Apex classes and write the missing tests yourself.

1. Setup recap (60 min)

  1. Authorize: sf org login web against your Dev Hub (00D... / default dev hub).
  2. Create scratch: sf org create scratch -f config/project-scratch-def.json
  3. Push: sf project deploy start
  4. Assign the Data360_Consultant permission set to your user.
  5. Verify the objects/services exist; run sf apex run on scripts/apex/hello.apex and scripts/soql/account.soql.

config/project-scratch-def.json requests orgName "Data Cloud Consultant RoadMap Lab", features for Data Cloud-labelled metadata (see the file), settings for AI/agent/prompt/Data Cloud settings flags the custom metadata expects, and API 68.0.

2. The signature labs (the 6 that matter)

For each: read the service, run the tests, then extend with a new scenario in a NEW test class. Do not skip test-writing — that's the consultant's proof-of-alignment.

#LabService under testWhat "done" looks like
L1Ingest canonical Stream__dlm payloadDataCloudIngestionServicePayload → normalized DLO records; scripts/apex/ingest_payload.apex runs
L2Identity match: CRM + DLO → unified IndividualIdIdentityResolutionHelperServiceMatch rules (SSN/phone/email/account) produce candidate set; Identity_Resolution_Candidate__c rows created
L3Segment membership mathSegmentMembershipServiceSegment_Sync_Log__c row recorded; list size asserted in test
L4Consent-suppress activationActivationSyncService3 sent / 2 suppressed / audit row written (Phase 7 numbers)
L5Churn insight → QoS alertCalculatedInsightService + DataActionHandlerServiceThreshold fires a Data_Action_Event__e; subscriber wrote the case update/audit
L6Enrich Case from profileUnifiedProfileEnrichmentServiceTrigger on Case writes lifetime-value/churn on create+update paths only for known profiles

Timed run (exam-style)

  • L1–L3: 45 min. L4–L6: 45 min. Total 90 of your 105-minute exam budget — practice the clock as much as the code.

3. Mini Project A — Consent-aware activation console

Goal: a repeatable path from consent capture to a suppressed activation.

Accepted scope: Apex + flows using ConsentManagementService, Consent_Preference__c, ActivationSyncService, and Activation_Audit__c.

Deliverables:

  1. ConsentManagementService.setConsent accepts (member key, 2 categories, opt-in) via flow or API; 1 DML per call (upsert), idempotent.
  2. ActivationSyncService.publishActivation(segmentName, List<Id> members, String consentCategory) returns the 3-number audit (qualified / sent / suppressed) and persists it.
  3. A test proving: withdraw → next publish excludes the member; retry path is idempotent (2 runs = same row count updated, no duplicates).

4. Mini Project B — Real-time churn handler

Goal: churn-score threshold crossing → CRM/notify side effect, imitating a Data Cloud-triggered flow.

Accepted scope: CalculatedInsightService (churnScore(), threshold check) + DataActionHandlerService + Data_Action_Event__e, all with a bulk subscribe handler (no per-record DML, Limits.getCallouts() guarded).

Deliverables:

  1. CalculatedInsightService.fireChurnActions(casesOrProfiles, Decimal threshold) publishes ONE event per crossing member in a single EventBus.publish(batch) call.
  2. Event subscriber (DataActionEventSubscriberTrigger) delegates to DataActionHandlerService and runs exactly once per event (recursion guard).
  3. Test: 50 members, 12 cross threshold → exactly 12 events published, exactly 12 audit rows, MOST_RECURRENT/limits respected.

5. Mini Project C — Agentforce grounding context

Goal: a narrow, safe Apex action that returns a Data-Graph-style JSON node for an agent.

Accepted scope: AgentforceBillingContextService (from Phase 14 Exercise 4) + test.

Deliverables:

  1. @InvocableMethod takes {IndividualKey, requestedFields} → returns exactly the requested fields as a dense JSON node (no table dumping).
  2. Unknown key → graceful {"error":"profile-not-found"} node, no exception to the agent.
  3. Test asserts: field whitelist enforced, JSON valid, callouts guarded.

6. Grading rubric (use it)

LevelEvidence
PassAll tests green; coverage ≥ 75% on the class you touched; no DML-in-loop
Pass++ you extended the service with a new scenario test AND documented it in ARCHITECTURE.md
Distinction+ you wired a flow/trigger to consume the new capability (tour of Lightning state)

Hands-On Exercises

Exercise 1: Coverage audit

Run sf project deploy start then sf apex test run ; report the per-class coverage table. Find the class under quota and add tests until each newly-written class is ≥ 90%.

Exercise 2: 90-minute timed run

Run the L1–L6 battery against the clock. Record where you spent time; re-run the slowest lab the next day ≤ 60% of original time.

Exercise 3: Self-grade

Grade yourself against the rubric table above and write the 3 things that would move Mini Project B to "Pass+" (design ideas only, no code changes unless you want).

Key Terms Glossary

TermDefinition
Signature labs (L1–L6)The six service/test pairs proving the ingestion→profile→segment→activation→action→enrich spine.
Timed batteryThe 90-min lab run practicing exam time-budgeting.
Mini projectA scope-bounded build (consent activation / churn handler / agent context) with deliverables + rubric.
Coverage ≥ 75%Salesforce's gate for change-scoped Apex in production; your scratch-org grail.
Subject-matter alignmentTests that assert business rules (3 sent / 2 suppressed), not just "no exceptions".

Certification Checkpoints

  • I can deploy the repo to a scratch org and run all signature labs.
  • I pass the L1–L6 timed battery within 90 minutes.
  • Mini projects A, B, C each have green tests + documented design.
  • Every class I authored in this repo has ≥ 90% coverage or an accepted exception.

Self-Check

  1. Q: Which single rule prevents the classic activation bug in Mini A? — A: Idempotent upsert by the member's external key + the consent suppression before the publish (so counts are consistent across reruns).
  2. Q: What is the bulk discipline in Mini B's subscriber? — A: One EventBus.publish(batch) for all 12 crossings, single delegate, recursion guard, one audit batch — never per-record DML.
  3. Q: Why return only requestedFields in Mini C? — A: Token economy + least-privilege: an agent should never receive profile data it didn't ask for.
